beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The Right to Help questions when an attempt to improve lives becomes a claim over them.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The human author’s wish to help meets an artificial voice instructed to challenge its assurances.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That voice is a literary instrument, not an oracle with proven inner experience.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book examines help through the recipient’s power as well as the helper’s intention.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Readers encounter an inquiry that makes both intervention and comfortable inaction answerable.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A helpful intervention changes who can refuse, wait, decide, and later describe what happened.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Consent becomes difficult when the alternative to accepting help is serious deprivation.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book also follows interests that lose money or authority when suffering is reduced.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: These conflicts prevent a simple division between generous helpers and ungrateful recipients.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The examples support a deeper question about who can challenge the shape of an intervention.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Later chapters examine power acquired for good and then preserved by redefining the good.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The proposed response includes criticism, repair, meaningful refusal, and the return of authority.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: No final moral algorithm removes the disagreements about benefit, risk, or legitimate limits.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book keeps emergencies and the harms of doing nothing inside the argument.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its possible constitution remains unfinished because the people affected must retain a real voice.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Begin with the trial of good before turning to the proposed constitution of legitimate help.
